AND the stage carries on' is true for every `Exception`, which is the whole of what compilation raises from a file. It is not true for a BaseException, and one BaseException is genuinely reachable during a long compile: a SIGINT delivered while source_to_code is running raises KeyboardInterrupt out of the try and kills the stage (measured, returncode -2, exit 130 through the gate wiring, so fail-closed and identical in kind to interrupting the old loop). The carve-out is stated at :92 to :94, in the docstring, rather than in the preserved-properties list at :15. I rate the sentence PROVED rather than overstated, because a user interrupt is not a property of a file, and I record the placement only because that list is what a later reader will narrow the handler against. The limit clause itself, `a failure that kills the process outright, a signal or the OOM killer, is named by nothing, and the stage's non-zero exit is what the gate reads', is TRUE AND SUFFICIENT on my measurement: 139 for SIGSEGV, 137 for SIGKILL, 134 for a fatal interpreter error, 130 for SIGINT, all RED.

N8 THE ONE-PROCESS DESIGN RAISES PEAK MEMORY AND DOES NOT ACCUMULATE, WHICH IS WHY THE OOM ASYMMETRY IS DECLARABLE RATHER THAN BLOCKING. Under the per-file loop an OOM-killed child was a NAMED per-file failure with continuation, because the shell saw a non-zero child and printed its FAIL line; under one process the OOM killer takes the whole stage and nothing is named. That asymmetry is real and is what the declared limit covers. I measured the exposure rather than leaving it as a worry: peak RSS of the whole stage over the real 694-file corpus is 104888 KB (`/usr/bin/time -f %M`), the compiled code objects are discarded rather than retained, and compiling each of five poison shapes twenty times in one process leaves a valid file compiling correctly afterwards every time with no residual growth beyond the high-water mark of the largest single compile. So there is no cross-contamination and no leak, and 104 MB is not a plausible OOM at this corpus size. Worth revisiting only if the corpus grows by an order of magnitude or a single tracked file becomes very large.

residual_rulings.THE RESIDUAL ISOLATION GAP - can a corpu: NO HARD CRASH FOUND, AND THE DECLARED LIMIT IS TRUE AND FAILS CLOSED. I put 49 pathological shapes through SourceFileLoader.source_to_code in a fresh process each, with a marker printed after the handler so survival is observable rather than inferred. NOT ONE segfaulted, aborted, or produced a fatal interpreter error, and all 49 printed the marker. The families I tried: operator chains to 1,000,000 terms (unary minus, invert, not, and, or, comparison, matmul, binop, string concatenation, ternary); paren, bracket and brace nesting to 100,000; attribute, call, subscript and slice chains to 200,000; nested f-strings and PEP 701 nested format specs; PEP 695 `type X[T]` aliases nested 100,000 deep and 50,000 wide; match statements and deep match patterns; except* groups; nested lambdas, generator expressions, set comprehensions and yields; 100,000 levels of indentation and 50,000 nested classes; 200,000 stacked decorators; a 10 MB string literal; a 5,000,000-digit integer literal; 300,000 statements; and 100,000 chained assignment targets. Outcomes were SyntaxError, IndentationError, RecursionError, MemoryError or a clean compile, every one an `Exception` subclass, which is exactly what the widened handler exists to catch. THE CONSTRUCTIONS MOST LIKELY TO CRASH ARE THE ONES CPython 3.12 SPECIFICALLY GUARDS: the tokenizer's MAXLEVEL turns deep bracket nesting into SyntaxError before the C stack is reached, MAXINDENT does the same for indentation, and the 3.12 C-recursion budget turns parser and compiler recursion into RecursionError or MemoryError rather than a stack overflow. THEN I RULED THE LIMIT ITSELF by forcing the deaths the builder says are named by nothing, injected inside check_python's try so they happen mid-corpus: SIGSEGV via ctypes gives -11 direct and 139 through the shell, SIGKILL gives -9 and 137, Py_FatalError gives -6 and 134, KeyboardInterrupt gives -2 and 130. verify.sh runs the stage as `if bash -c "$cmd"` with stdout inherited, no pipeline anywhere, and check_lint.sh uses `exec python3 - <<'PY'` so the interpreter's status IS the script's status: I ran the exact `if bash -c` shape and it took the RED branch for all four. THE ONE EXIT-0 DEATH IS `SystemExit(0)`, which gives rc 0, no output, and the GREEN branch. It is NOT REACHABLE, and I verified reachability rather than reasoning about it: `SourceFileLoader.source_to_code` is `compile()` with dont_inherit, so a file containing `import sys` and `sys.exit(0)`, or `raise SystemExit(0)`, or `exec('import sys; sys.exit(0)')` COMPILES CLEAN with no execution; nothing in the stage's own machinery inside the try can raise SystemExit; and the only interpreter-side hook a file controls is the coding cookie, whose lookup is confined to the encodings package and which produced a plain SyntaxError for every hostile value I gave it (`rot13`, an unknown name, `os.path`, `../../etc/passwd`). SO: no hard crash from a file, and if one is ever found it goes RED. KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit and GeneratorExit are confirmed NOT `Exception` subclasses, which is why I checked each of them separately rather than trusting the class hierarchy in prose.
residual_rulings.DOES `except Exception` NOW SWALLOW SOME: NO, AND THERE IS NO REGRESSION AGAINST THE DESIGN IT REPLACED, WHICH IS THE ONLY FAIR BAR. The try block holds three things and nothing else: `open(path, "rb")`, `fh.read()`, and `SourceFileLoader(...).source_to_code(data, path)`. There is no harness LOGIC inside it to go wrong, which is the structural reason the widening cannot overshoot far. I INJECTED FOUR DEFECTS AND MEASURED ALL FOUR. A path typo in the harness (`path = path + "X"`) names all 694 files on their own FAIL lines, prints `lint: FAIL (694 python, 172 shell, 0.11s)`, exits 1, and puts `FileNotFoundError` on stderr for each. A TypeError in the harness (an extra positional argument to source_to_code) does the same with `TypeError` on stderr. A defect OUTSIDE the try (`git ls-filez`) exits 1 with a traceback, no path named and no summary. A harness-side decode change that happens to be behaviourally equivalent for this corpus passes, and on a non-ASCII file would raise UnicodeDecodeError and name that file, a FALSE RED. SO A SYSTEMATIC HARNESS BUG CANNOT REPORT A FILE AS PASSING; it reports all 694 as failing, which is loud, RED, and per-path. A TOOL DEFECT IS DISTINGUISHABLE FROM A FILE DEFECT by the exception class the stage prints at scripts/check_lint.sh:102 (`<path>: <ExcName>: <msg>`): a file defect gives the syntax and OS families, a tool defect gives TypeError, AttributeError, NameError or FileNotFoundError across the entire corpus at once. Nothing ASSERTS that distinction and there is no distinct exit code for it, which I considered and rejected as a finding, because py_compile did EXACTLY the same thing (its own `except Exception` turned any harness fault into a PyCompileError and a named per-file failure) so the round-1 baseline had the identical property, and because the failure mode is a false RED rather than a false GREEN. Round 1's lesson was a handler whose width was WRONG; this correction lands on py_compile's own width and stops there, rather than on BaseException.

ELEVEN DIED. M2 delete the parser-stack fixture: 2 fail. M3 delete the deep-nesting fixture: 2 fail. M4 RENAME BOTH POISON FIXTURES TO SORT LAST so `_L07_AFTER_POISON` becomes the empty list: 2 FAIL, INCLUDING THE CONTINUATION ASSERTION. That is the direct refutation of the rot the prompt predicted: `_L07_AFTER_POISON != []` is a CONJUNCT of the expect, so an empty set makes the assertion FAIL rather than pass vacuously. M5 stage drops the summary line: 4 fail including the continuation assertion, so the summary conjunct is behaviourally teethed. M6 a second `except Exception as e:` in the stage: the uniqueness conjunct fails, so the mutation target cannot silently match nothing or match twice. M7 neutralize the SIGPIPE restoration: 1 fails, closing round-1's only surviving mutation. M8 first-error-wins by breaking out of the loop: 4 fail. M11 handler widened to BaseException: the uniqueness conjunct fails (see N4). M13 name the poison but skip every later file: 4 fail. THE TWO SURVIVORS ARE BOTH DELETIONS OF ASSERTION TEXT, NOT BEHAVIOUR CHANGES: M9 rewriting `_L07_AFTER_POISON != []` as `(_L07_AFTER_POISON != [] or True)` and M12 removing the summary-line conjunct from the continuation expect. Any assertion can be deleted by editing it; what matters is whether the property it guards is detectable when it actually breaks, and M4 and M5 prove it is. THE EXPECTATIONS ARE ENUMERATED RATHER THAN COMPUTED FROM THE CODE UNDER TEST: `_L07_POISON` is a literal tuple of two names, `len(_L07_POISON) == 2` and `len(_L07_MUST_FAIL) == 8` are literals against a fixture dictionary declared in the same file, and the must-fail set comes from the fixture DECLARATION rather than from the stage's output, which is why M2 and M3 die on a deletion.
residual_rulings.IS THE PLACEMENT ASSERTION REALLY NOT A: NOT A PIN, PROVEN BY DOING THE CORRECTION AND RUNNING THE WHOLE GATE. In a detached worktree at d4addf8 I changed specs/WARP-0711-lint-one-interpreter.md:22 from `placement: [engine]` to `placement: [enforcement]`, the exact correction the manifest asks the owner to make, and ran `/usr/bin/time -v ./scripts/verify.sh` to completion: GATE: GREEN, exit 0, 3:11.44 wall clock, 3195 passed / 0 failed, catalog 5 run / 18 not-applicable / 0 waived / 0 undeclared, and ZERO WARP-0711 assertions failed. disposition: LAND IT. Round 1 failed this item on one real code defect and one record defect, and both are closed at the right level: the handler width is now TAKEN from py_compile rather than chosen, which is the difference between a fix and a patch, and the false sentence was replaced by what is asserted with its limit written beside it rather than reworded. I attacked the residual isolation gap harder than anything else, because a declared limit is where a reviewer should be most suspicious, and it survived: 49 pathological shapes give no hard crash on this interpreter, every hard death I could force goes RED through the gate's own wiring, and the one exit-0 death is unreachable because compilation does not execute code. The widening did not overshoot, every injected tool defect fails closed and names its class, eleven of thirteen mutations die with the two survivors being deletions of assertion text, the after-poison set fails closed rather than rotting into a vacuous pass, and correcting the placement declaration keeps the whole gate green at 3195 passed / 0 failed. Every figure re-derives at its stated revision, including the B2 three-stage result and the 3191/4 split to the assertion, which is exactly what round 1 asked for. THE TEN NOTES ARE NOTES, AND ONE OF THEM DESERVES AN ITEM: WARP_LINT_LIST=1 in the gate's environment makes the stage exit 0 having checked nothing, which turned a tree with six planted defects GREEN in my measurement. It is unreachable from anything the gate reads and set nowhere on a gate path, so it does not block this item, but a gate stage should not carry an environment switch that can be mistaken for a pass, and the closure is one line. THE THREE SPEC DEFECTS REMAIN THE OWNER'S: (a) delete the AC3 engine-canon clause and the two dead footprint globs or open a promotion item, (b) correct `placement: [engine]` to `placement: [enforcement]`, which I have now PROVEN costs nothing, and (c) date the corpus figure rather than renumber it. Nothing mechanical will notice if (b) is never done, which is the honest price of unpinning it and is now on the record. A faster lint that misses an error class is a defect; this one does not miss an error class any more, and I tried hard to find one it misses.
